headline_tag: Uptrend holds as price rests just above its 50-day line

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's call is to scale up the acquisition budget: the longer-term trend and the last three months both lean up, with high confidence (82/100 including today's news, 79 on market data alone), so this is a reasonable time to fund growth, weighted toward channels that bring active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price is resting just above its 50-day average and the Fed decides on 27 October, grow the budget in steps and keep part of it flexible to pause if price closes below $81,507 (the 50-day average). This is a budget posture based on trailing data, not a price call or trading advice.

watch: The longer picture leans up, but price is less than 1% above its 50-day average ($81,507) while US Bitcoin funds saw about $487M leave on the latest day and Asian stocks opened sharply lower. A close below $81,507 would test the uptrend; a move back above $86,603 would ease the worry.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger picture still leans up, but this week looks like a pause rather than a push. Short term, the mood is only mildly warm: the Fear & Greed reading is 59 out of 100, US Bitcoin funds saw about $487M leave on the latest day, and Asian stocks opened sharply lower on Monday (South Korea down 3%, per PANews). If price closes above $86,603 (the 30-day high) the short-term picture turns clearly up; below $81,507 (the 50-day average) it turns down, and in between expect choppy days. Fresh fund inflows would firm this up and another weak day for stocks would cool it, so steady rather than loud campaigns fit this week.

Over the next month, the picture leans gently up. Price is about 24% higher than three months ago and roughly 69% of the last 90 days closed above the long-term average, but the past week has been flat. There is room to climb if price gets above $86,603 (the 90-day high); the move starts to fade if price slips below $81,507 (the 50-day average), which is less than 1% under today's level. The Fed's 27 October decision is the next scheduled event that could tip this; a clean hold above the 50-day line would keep growth campaigns well timed.

Over three to six months, the trend leans up with the most confidence of the three. Price is about 13% above its 200-day average, but that average is still flat to slightly falling and price remains 34% below its record, so this is an early recovery, not a mature uptrend. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,577 (the 200-day average); $66,796 (the 200-week average) is the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) is the far marker. A rising 200-day average would confirm it, while slow steps toward official adoption, such as Latvia's plan to accept crypto for income tax from 2027 (PANews), are background support rather than a driver.
